note: Starts with modern kobzar-revival recordings, then goes back to the 1908–1910 wax cylinders of the last traditional kobzari and lirnyky, which are crackly but real. Titles are printed as their sources print them, in English or in Latin-letter Ukrainian.

size.basis: Repertoire is small: dumy are a closed set of Cossack-era subjects (the Encyclopedia of Ukraine names six as examples; the 1908–1910 cylinders hold about a dozen subjects). Archive side: the Kolessa/Slastion/Kvitka cylinder collection on Commons has 24 duma rows, plus later Soviet-era field and radio recordings of the few surviving traditional kobzari not counted here. Revival side: a few dozen kobzar-revival performers (Kytasty, Kushpet, Fedynsky, Kompanichenko, Drach, the kobzar guilds), each recording a handful of dumy. The range is a judgement, not a catalogue total; core = the dozen classic subjects in one or two good recordings each.
